text:
Alice (Acme): Hey team — since the model bump to redwood-v3.2.1 last night, our in-app assistant answers are noticeably shorter and omit follow-ups. Example attached. Anyone else seeing a subtle brevity shift?

jordan_support: Thanks for flagging, Alice. Can you paste one full request/response pair and tell us if you're using hosted or private?

Alice (Acme): hosted. Here's a minimal repro (old model vs new):

```
# OLD
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v3.1.8","input":"How do I reset my password?","max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.2}'

# response excerpt:
"To reset your password, go to Settings > Account > Reset Password. We'll email a link. If you don't see it, check spam."

# NEW
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v3.2.1","input":"How do I reset my password?","max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.2}'

# response excerpt:
"Go to Settings > Account > Reset Password and follow the link."
```

jordan_support: That looks like a consistent truncation — fewer details. Thanks for including both payloads. @priya_ml any quick theories?

priya_ml: pinging ML team. Two quick suspects: (1) model fine-tune objective introduced brevity weighting or changed LM head; (2) decoding defaults changed (e.g., new response length priors or different stop token handling). Also check if system prompt got shorter in rollout config. Can you share request_id(s)?

Alice (Acme): request ids: r-20260302-82a and r-20260302-93b. We captured them from our logs.

mike_prod: deploy-bot shows rollout of redwood-v3.2.1 completed at 2026-03-01T22:45Z across hosted clusters. Canary was 10% for 2hrs then ramped. No config override noted in deploy notes but I'll pull the release diff.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-v3.2.1 -> complete (2026-03-01T22:45Z)

jordan_support: OK opening an internal escalation (INC-2026-224). Assigning @priya_ml and @mike_prod. Mitigations: short-term—encourage customer to force max_tokens=200 or add "Please explain in 3-4 sentences" to system prompt; we'll see if that restores length.

priya_ml: For repro locally, please run both models with identical seed and decoding params. Quick curl to compare:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-v3.1.8","input":"Explain X","max_tokens":120,"temperature":0.0,"top_p":0.9}'
# then swap model to redwood-v3.2.1
```

priya_ml: I'll run A/B with decoding params and check token-level logprobs. If it's model-level (loss or fine-tune), we'll need a rollback for hosted and a fast patch. If it's decoding defaults, we can revert the change without model changes.

mike_prod: Found a small change in the serving config: default "response_penalty=0.1" introduced in rollout pipeline. That could bias brevity. Rolling to a staging cluster to test removing penalty now.

jordan_support: Thanks. Alice, we'll keep you updated. Short-term workaround: add explicit length instruction or set max_tokens higher.

Alice (Acme): Thanks — we'll try the prompt tweak and report back. Appreciate quick help.

priya_ml: Update: removing response_penalty on staging makes outputs match previous length in preliminary tests. Next: confirm across multiple prompts and run regen testset. If confirmed, we'll publish a fix to hosted defaults and schedule a postmortem.

mike_prod: If fix is ok, we can push a config rollback within the hour and monitor Latency/Cost metrics.

jordan_support: Next steps: PR to revert default penalty, run regression tests, coordinate rollback window, notify customers. I'll send status updates to the thread and set ETA for 1h.

priya_ml: Noted — I'll prepare evaluation diffs and token-level plots to include in postmortem.

jordan_support: Closing loop here once rollback done. :thumbsup:
